title: Pawn races: the square, and who queens first
outcomes: Decides whether a lone king can catch a passed pawn by drawing the pawn's square
Counts a two-pawn race and sees when the first queen wins the other pawn
Names two ways the square rule misleads: your own king's help and a pawn on its second rank

steps.text: Can a lone king catch a runaway pawn? Count the pawn's steps to the eighth rank and draw a square with that many squares on a side, starting at the pawn. If the defending king is inside the square, or steps into it on his move, he catches the pawn. This **rule of the square** is a heuristic: it counts only the pawn and the defending king.

steps.caption: Black to move. His king cannot get into the pawn's square in time.

line.say: Black's king heads for the pawn's path.
The pawn steps forward and the square shrinks.
Black's king takes another step towards the pawn.
Black's king is still a step too far.
The pawn reaches the seventh rank.
Black's king reaches d7, one file too far to touch b8.

claims.statement: With Black to move, Black loses.

steps.text: **The square rule has limits.** (1) Your own king can escort the pawn, so a king inside the square may still lose. (2) A pawn on its second rank can move two squares. In a **race** of two pawns, count both: the side that queens first is not automatically winning, so check what the new queen attacks.

steps.title: One tempo
steps.prompt: The pawn is on b4, White's king far away on h1, Black's king on g6. White to move, or Black to move? Predict each result, then check.

steps.caption: A race: White's a-pawn against Black's h-pawn. White has just queened on a8. Black to move.

line.say: Black queens too, with check along the first rank.
White's queen takes it along the long diagonal.

claims.statement: With Black to move, Black loses.
The white queen on a8 attacks h1.

steps.title: Same race, different file
steps.prompt: Each pawn needs three moves, White moves first. Does White still win if the pawn is on the b-file? Predict, then check.
When you predicted, which did you count first: the pawn's steps, the king's steps, or the move? Which one did you forget in the position where you were wrong?
